schema_info.description: One row per schema version applied to this database, recording which version of the relational model the file carries and when it was installed.

schema_version.description: Version label of the applied schema. Agrees with the header of schema/schema.sql, this table's seeded row, and PRAGMA user_version; a check enforces that all three match.

applied_at_utc.description: UTC timestamp recorded when VAWLUME applied this schema version to the database. An audit time, not an observation time from the research data.

description.description: Free-text note shipped alongside the schema version seed, summarizing what changed in that version.

projects.description: A research project: the outermost scope that owns recordings, experimental entities, source files, and the configuration profiles under which their source material is interpreted.

project_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for the project, generated by the database and meaningful only inside this file.

project_key.description: Caller-supplied stable identifier for the project, unique within the database and declared explicitly at intake rather than inferred from the source hierarchy. This is the project's durable identity, so it survives a database rebuild in a way project_id does not.

project_name.description: Human-readable name for the project, used when reporting results to a person.

description.description: Free-text account of what the project covers. Never parsed by VAWLUME.

created_at_utc.description: UTC timestamp recorded when VAWLUME created this row. An audit time, not a fact about when the research took place.

archived_at_utc.description: UTC timestamp recorded when the project was archived. Null while the project is still active.

config_profiles.description: A named configuration profile: one interpretation contract, such as how a project's directory structure is read or how an extractor's output columns are understood. Rows elsewhere cite a profile version to record the assumptions under which they were produced.

profile_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for the configuration profile, generated by the database.

project_id.description: Project that owns this profile. Null for a profile shipped with VAWLUME, which is available to every project in the database.

profile_key.description: Stable identifier for the profile, supplied by the profile document rather than generated. Together with the profile kind it forms the profile's durable identity, and it is unique within its project.

profile_name.description: Human-readable name for the profile, used when reporting which configuration produced a result.

profile_kind.description: Which interpretation contract this profile expresses, drawn from a declared vocabulary that separates source and project mapping, extractor output and settings, recording device, experimental setup, tracking and attribution input mapping, analysis settings, and policy. The kinds are deliberately distinct so that one profile cannot silently take on another's responsibility.

is_builtin.description: Whether VAWLUME shipped this profile (1) or a user authored it (0). Built-in profiles are seeded from the repository rather than registered from a user document.

description.description: Free-text account of what the profile interprets and under what assumptions. Never parsed by VAWLUME.

created_at_utc.description: UTC timestamp recorded when VAWLUME created this row. An audit time, not a property of the profile document.

config_profile_versions.description: One registered version of a configuration profile, carrying where its document was read from and a digest of its contents, so that any row citing this version can be traced back to the exact document that was in force when it was written.

profile_version_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for this profile version, generated by the database. This is what other tables cite when they record which configuration governed them.

profile_id.description: Configuration profile that this is a version of.

version_label.description: Version as authored in the profile document itself. Unique within its profile and part of the version's durable identity, so republishing changed content under an existing label is refused rather than accepted.

profile_schema_version.description: Which revision of the profile document grammar this version was written against, as distinct from the version of the profile's own content. Null when the document declares none.

content_format.description: Serialization of the registered document, normally inferred from its file extension. VAWLUME's own configuration is JSON; the other permitted values exist so an externally authored document can be registered and cited without first being rewritten.

content_uri.description: Where the profile document was read from, stored repository-relative when the file lives under the repository root and absolute otherwise. The file is hashed, never copied, so this records a location rather than custody of the bytes.

checksum_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the profile document as registered. Re-registering this same version label over different bytes is reported as a conflict, because rows already cite this version by identifier and changing what it denotes would silently re-point their provenance.

is_snapshot.description: Caller-declared flag recording whether the registered content is a fixed snapshot rather than a reference expected to change underneath it. Defaults to true and is a statement about the document, not something VAWLUME verifies.

created_at_utc.description: UTC timestamp recorded when VAWLUME registered this version. An audit time, not the date the profile was authored.

notes.description: Free-text remarks about this particular version. Never parsed by VAWLUME.

project_profile_assignments.description: Records that a configuration profile version applies to a project in a named role, which is how a project declares the defaults its recordings can inherit.

project_id.description: Project the profile version is assigned to.

profile_version_id.description: Exact profile version being assigned. A version, not a profile, so the assignment records which content was in force.

assignment_role.description: The role this profile version plays for the project. The same version can be assigned in more than one role, so the role is part of the assignment's identity rather than a label on it.

is_default.description: Whether this assignment is the project default for its role, and therefore a candidate for inheritance onto recordings that declare no assignment of their own.

assigned_at_utc.description: UTC timestamp recorded when VAWLUME created this assignment. An audit time.

source_files.description: A file VAWLUME discovered and registered as project source material, identified by its location within the project rather than by its absolute runtime path, so that relocating a project root reuses the same rows.

source_file_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for the registered file, generated by the database.

project_id.description: Project this file was discovered within.

file_role.description: What this file is to the project, such as the audio a recording was made from or an artifact an extractor produced. It records how the file was claimed rather than what format it happens to be.

path_or_uri.description: Location the file was discovered at, as discovered, and unique within its project. Absolute runtime paths are used to prove a file exists for one execution and are deliberately not what intake treats as identity.

relative_path.description: Normalized portable path of the file within the project root. Together with the project this is what intake treats as the file's durable identity, which is why relocating a project root reuses the same rows rather than registering the files again.

filename.description: Base name of the file, separated out so that files sharing a name in different folders remain distinguishable while still being searchable by name.

file_format.description: Format of the file as recorded at discovery, normally derived from its extension. Not verified by reading the file.

size_bytes.description: Size of the file in bytes at discovery. Null when discovery did not record it.

checksum_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the file's contents at registration. Relocating the file is recognised as the same file; a change to its contents is a conflict rather than an overwrite. Null when no digest was taken.

source_modified_at.description: Modification time as reported by the source, in whatever form the source expressed it. Deliberately not recorded as UTC: VAWLUME does not know the zone it was expressed in and will not assert one.

discovered_at_utc.description: UTC timestamp recorded when VAWLUME registered this file. An audit time, and distinct from the file's own modification time.

ingestion_runs.description: One attempt to ingest a project's source material under a particular mapping profile version. Successful reruns create new rows rather than rewriting earlier ones, so the history of attempts survives even when the resulting graph is unchanged.

ingestion_run_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for this ingestion attempt, generated by the database.

mapping_profile_version_id.description: Exact project-input mapping profile version that interpreted the sources for this attempt. This is what makes the resulting rows traceable to the rules that produced them.

run_label.description: Optional caller-supplied label distinguishing this attempt from others. Free text with no uniqueness requirement.

vawlume_version.description: Version of VAWLUME the caller asserted was in use. Supplied by the caller and never inferred from the working tree, so it records a claim rather than a verified fact.

source_commit.description: Source revision the caller asserted was in use. Like the version, a caller claim that VAWLUME records without checking.

status.description: State of the attempt, drawn from a declared vocabulary that separates one still in progress from one that completed, one that completed with warnings, and one that failed. Warnings are not errors and the distinction is kept.

started_at_utc.description: UTC timestamp recorded when the attempt began.

completed_at_utc.description: UTC timestamp recorded when the attempt finished. Null while the attempt is unfinished or if it never reached a terminal state.

log_uri.description: Location of an external log for this attempt, when the caller recorded one. VAWLUME stores the reference and does not read it.

notes.description: Free-text remarks about this attempt. Never parsed by VAWLUME.

ingestion_files.description: Records how one source file fared in one ingestion attempt, so that a run's outcome can be read per file rather than only in aggregate.

ingestion_run_id.description: Ingestion attempt this outcome belongs to.

source_file_id.description: Source file this outcome is about.

parse_status.description: How this file fared in this attempt, drawn from a declared vocabulary that separates a file not yet reached, a clean parse, a parse with warnings, a file deliberately skipped, and a failure. Skipped and failed are different outcomes and are kept apart.

warning_count.description: Number of warnings raised while parsing this file in this attempt. Zero means none were raised, not that none were possible.

error_count.description: Number of errors raised while parsing this file in this attempt.

parser_message.description: Human-readable summary of what the parser reported for this file. Diagnostic text, not a structured issue record.

entity_types.description: One level of a project's own experimental hierarchy, such as its notion of a cohort, a subject, or a session, registered under the project's native name for it and optionally mapped to a canonical role VAWLUME understands.

entity_type_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for this hierarchy level, generated by the database.

project_id.description: Project whose hierarchy this level belongs to. Levels are project-scoped because two projects may use the same word for different things.

native_name.description: The project's own name for this level, preserved as the source expressed it. Unique within the project and part of the level's durable identity.

canonical_role.description: The role this level is declared to fill, such as a study, a subject, or a session. An open vocabulary rather than a fixed one, so a project can declare a role VAWLUME does not model natively. This is the added canonical reading; the native name remains the source's own. Null when no canonical role was declared.

hierarchy_order.description: Where this level sits in the project's declared nesting, as the project ordered it. VAWLUME stores the ordering and neither computes nor enforces it. Null when the project declared no ordering.

is_biological_unit.description: Whether entities at this level are biological individuals rather than organizational groupings. Declared by the project, not inferred from the level's name.

is_subject_like.description: Whether entities at this level behave as subjects for analysis purposes. Kept separate from the biological flag because the two can disagree: an organizational unit may be analysed as a subject, and a biological individual may not be the unit of analysis.

description.description: Free-text account of what this level represents in the project. Never parsed by VAWLUME.

experimental_entities.description: One thing in a project's experimental hierarchy — a particular cohort, subject, or session — identified by the project's own name for it at its own level.

entity_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for this entity, generated by the database.

entity_type_id.description: Hierarchy level this entity sits at, which is what makes its native identifier interpretable.

native_id.description: The project's own identifier for this entity, preserved as the source expressed it. Unique within its level, and together with the level it forms the entity's durable identity.

display_label.description: Human-readable label for the entity when the native identifier is not itself readable. Null when none was supplied.

ingestion_run_id.description: Ingestion attempt that first created this row. Later compatible attempts record their own audit rows rather than rewriting this provenance, so this names the attempt the entity entered the database on.

created_at_utc.description: UTC timestamp recorded when VAWLUME created this row. An audit time, not a fact about the experiment.

entity_relationships.description: A declared relationship between two entities in a project's hierarchy, most often containment, together with the source evidence and mapping rule that produced it. An entity may not be related to itself.

entity_relationship_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for this relationship, generated by the database.

parent_entity_id.description: The containing or superior entity of the pair. Which endpoint is the parent is part of the relationship's meaning, not an arbitrary ordering.

child_entity_id.description: The contained or subordinate entity of the pair, and never the same entity as the parent.

relationship_type.description: What the relationship asserts between the two endpoints, defaulting to containment. Free text so a project can declare a relationship VAWLUME does not model natively.

role_label.description: The role the child plays in this relationship when the type alone is not specific enough. Part of the relationship's durable identity, so the same pair can be related more than once in different roles.

valid_from_utc.description: UTC time from which this relationship is asserted to hold. Null when the relationship is not time-bounded at its start.

valid_to_utc.description: UTC time until which this relationship is asserted to hold. Null when the relationship is open-ended.

ingestion_run_id.description: Ingestion attempt that first created this row. Null when the relationship did not arise from an ingestion attempt.

source_file_id.description: Source file this relationship was read from, when it came from one. Null when the relationship has no single originating file.

source_locator.description: Where within the source this relationship was read from, recorded so the assertion can be traced back to the text that produced it.

mapping_rule_key.description: Which rule in the mapping profile claimed this relationship, so the interpretation is traceable to the rule that made it rather than only to the profile as a whole.

entity_attributes.description: One attribute of one entity, stored in a typed column chosen by its declared value type, together with the source location and mapping rule it came from. Values reach this table because a mapping rule claimed them as attributes, not because they appeared in a source file.

entity_attribute_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for this attribute row, generated by the database.

attribute_name.description: The attribute's name as the source expressed it, preserved rather than normalized.

value_type.description: Which of the typed value columns carries this attribute's value, or the declared absence of a value. A constraint enforces that exactly one typed column is populated, and that none is when the value is absent, so a missing value can never be confused with an empty one.

value_text.description: The attribute's value when it is textual, and null otherwise.

value_real.description: The attribute's value when it is a real number, and null otherwise.

value_integer.description: The attribute's value when it is an integer, and null otherwise.

value_boolean.description: The attribute's value when it is a truth value, stored as 0 or 1, and null otherwise.

value_json.description: The attribute's value when it is a structured payload, stored as JSON text, and null otherwise.

unit.description: Unit the source expressed the value in, as the source expressed it. Free text that VAWLUME records and never interprets or converts.

ingestion_run_id.description: Ingestion attempt that first created this row. Null when the attribute did not arise from an ingestion attempt.

source_file_id.description: Source file this attribute was read from, when it came from one.

source_locator.description: Where within the source this value was read from, recorded so it can be traced back to the text it came from.

mapping_rule_key.description: Which rule in the mapping profile claimed this value, so the interpretation is traceable to the rule that made it.

recordings.description: One audio recording, anchored to exactly one registered source file. That anchor is the boundary extractor imports resolve against, so a recording is identified by the file it was made from rather than by any name an extractor gives it.

recording_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for the recording, generated by the database.

source_file_id.description: The registered audio file this recording is made from, unique across recordings. This one-to-one anchor is the recording's durable identity and the point extractor importers attach their runs to.

native_recording_id.description: The source's own identifier for this recording, preserved as expressed. Null when the source names recordings only by filename.

checksum_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the audio as registered. Null in the ordinary case, because intake does not open audio files; it is populated only when some adapter supplied the digest.

sample_rate_hz.description: Sampling rate in hertz, when it is known. Null in the ordinary case: intake reads no audio metadata, so this is populated only when an adapter supplied it rather than being measured from the file.

bit_depth.description: Bits per sample, when it is known. Like the sampling rate, supplied rather than measured, and null when nothing supplied it.

channel_count.description: Number of channels the recording is declared to have, when it is known. Supplied rather than measured. A declared channel index above this count is refused; a recording declaring no count is not checked at all.

duration_s.description: Duration in seconds, when it is known. Supplied rather than measured, and null in the ordinary case.

recorded_start_utc.description: UTC time the recording is asserted to have started. An assertion about the world, unlike the audit timestamp on this row, and null when nothing asserted it.

created_at_utc.description: UTC timestamp recorded when VAWLUME created this row. An audit time, and not to be read as when the recording was made.

notes.description: Free-text remarks about the recording. Never parsed by VAWLUME.

recording_channels.description: One channel of one recording. A channel row is a caller assertion that the recording has that channel; nothing inspects the audio to confirm it, and the microphone that produced it is placed in space by a separate row.

recording_channel_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for this channel, generated by the database.

recording_id.description: Recording this channel belongs to. A channel belongs to exactly one recording, which is what makes anything attached to it session-specific.

channel_index.description: Position of this channel within the recording, counting from one, and unique within the recording. Refused when it exceeds a declared channel count.

channel_label.description: Human-readable label for the channel as the source named it. Null when the source named it only by index.

channel_role.description: What this channel is for, when the caller declared a role for it. Free text, and null when no role was declared.

recording_entity_links.description: Records that an entity took part in a recording in a named role, optionally over a bounded interval within it. This is how the experimental hierarchy reaches individual recordings.

recording_entity_link_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for this participation record, generated by the database.

recording_id.description: Recording the entity took part in.

link_type.description: The nature of the entity's involvement, defaulting to participation. Free text so a project can declare an involvement VAWLUME does not model natively, and part of the link's durable identity.

role_label.description: The role the entity played, when the link type alone is not specific enough. Part of the link's durable identity, so one entity can be linked to one recording more than once in different roles.

start_time_s.description: Seconds from the start of the recording at which the entity's involvement begins. Null when the involvement is not time-bounded, which is the ordinary case for a participant present throughout.

end_time_s.description: Seconds from the start of the recording at which the entity's involvement ends, never before the start. Null when the involvement is open-ended.

ingestion_run_id.description: Ingestion attempt that first created this row. Null when the link did not arise from an ingestion attempt.

recording_attributes.description: One attribute of one recording, stored in a typed column chosen by its declared value type, together with the source location and mapping rule it came from. The same typed-value shape as entity attributes, scoped to a recording rather than to a participant in the hierarchy.

recording_attribute_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for this attribute row, generated by the database.

attribute_name.description: The attribute's name as the source expressed it, preserved rather than normalized.

value_type.description: Which of the typed value columns carries this attribute's value, or the declared absence of a value. A constraint enforces that exactly one typed column is populated, and that none is when the value is absent, so a missing value can never be confused with an empty one.

value_text.description: The attribute's value when it is textual, and null otherwise.

value_real.description: The attribute's value when it is a real number, and null otherwise.

value_integer.description: The attribute's value when it is an integer, and null otherwise.

value_boolean.description: The attribute's value when it is a truth value, stored as 0 or 1, and null otherwise.

value_json.description: The attribute's value when it is a structured payload, stored as JSON text, and null otherwise.

unit.description: Unit the source expressed the value in, as the source expressed it. Free text that VAWLUME records and never interprets or converts.

ingestion_run_id.description: Ingestion attempt that first created this row. Null when the attribute did not arise from an ingestion attempt.

source_file_id.description: Source file this attribute was read from, when it came from one.

source_locator.description: Where within the source this value was read from, recorded so it can be traced back to the text it came from.

mapping_rule_key.description: Which rule in the mapping profile claimed this value, so the interpretation is traceable to the rule that made it.

entity_profile_assignments.description: Records that a configuration profile version applies to one entity in a named role, so that a subject or session can carry configuration its project default does not supply.

entity_id.description: Entity the profile version is assigned to.

profile_version_id.description: Exact profile version being assigned, so the assignment records which content was in force rather than only which profile.

assignment_role.description: The role this profile version plays for the entity. Part of the assignment's identity, so one version can be assigned in more than one role.

assigned_at_utc.description: UTC timestamp recorded when VAWLUME created this assignment. An audit time.

recording_profile_assignments.description: Records that a configuration profile version applies to one recording in a named role, and how the recording came to have it. This is where an inherited default becomes an explicit, readable fact about a particular recording.

recording_id.description: Recording the profile version is assigned to.

profile_version_id.description: Exact profile version being assigned, so the assignment records which content was in force.

assignment_role.description: The role this profile version plays for the recording. Part of the assignment's identity, so one version can be assigned in more than one role.

inheritance_source.description: How this recording came to have the assignment: declared directly on it, inherited from a project default, or inherited through an entity it is linked to. Recorded so that an inherited assignment is never mistaken for one the user declared.

assigned_at_utc.description: UTC timestamp recorded when VAWLUME created this assignment. An audit time.

recording_epochs.description: A named interval within a recording, such as a phase of a protocol, optionally nested inside another interval of the same recording. Epochs are declared or imported rather than detected by VAWLUME.

epoch_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for this interval, generated by the database.

parent_epoch_id.description: Enclosing interval, when this one is nested inside another of the same recording. Null for a top-level interval.

epoch_name.description: Name of the interval as declared. Together with the recording and the interval bounds it forms the epoch's durable identity.

epoch_type.description: What kind of interval this is, when the caller declared a kind. Free text, and null when none was declared.

start_time_s.description: Seconds from the start of the recording at which this interval begins.

end_time_s.description: Seconds from the start of the recording at which this interval ends, never before the start.

source.description: Where the interval came from, defaulting to manual declaration or import. VAWLUME does not detect epochs itself, so this records who said so.

source_file_id.description: Source file this interval was read from, when it was imported from one. Null when it was declared directly.

notes.description: Free-text remarks about the interval. Never parsed by VAWLUME.

coordinate_systems.description: A declared spatial frame that positions within a project are expressed in. Two spatial facts are comparable if and only if they cite this same frame by identifier; VAWLUME implements no transformation between frames, so structural similarity between two frames never makes them interchangeable.

coordinate_system_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for this frame, generated by the database. Comparability between two spatial facts is decided by comparing this identifier and nothing else.

project_id.description: Project this frame is declared for. Frames are project-scoped shared reference data, cited by anything positioned within the project.

coordinate_system_key.description: Stable identifier for the frame as the project names it, unique within the project.

coordinate_system_name.description: Human-readable name for the frame, used when reporting which space a position was expressed in.

dimensionality.description: Whether the frame is two- or three-dimensional. Two is the working case; three is representable and never required, and a height may only be recorded under a three-dimensional frame.

unit.description: Unit positions in this frame are expressed in, held on the frame so that two comparable facts cannot disagree about it. Free text that VAWLUME never interprets or converts: a pixel frame is legal and supports no real-distance computation, and pixels are never treated as a metric unit.

origin_description.description: Human-readable account of where the frame's origin sits. Provenance for a reader, never applied by any computation.

orientation_description.description: Human-readable account of how the frame's axes are oriented. Provenance for a reader, never applied by any computation.

notes.description: Free-text remarks about the frame. Never parsed by VAWLUME.

channel_placements.description: Where one recording channel's microphone was, expressed in one declared frame. The placement attaches to a channel rather than to a device or a setup profile, so it is specific to the session that channel belongs to and cannot claim a position outliving it.

channel_placement_id.description: VAWLUME surrogate key for this placement, generated by the database.

recording_channel_id.description: Channel whose microphone this places, at most one placement per channel. Because a channel belongs to exactly one recording, the placement is session-specific by construction.

coordinate_system_id.description: Frame the coordinates below are expressed in. A placement and the frame it cites must belong to the same project, and a cited frame cannot be deleted while a placement still names it.

position_x.description: Position along the frame's first axis, in the frame's declared unit.

position_y.description: Position along the frame's second axis, in the frame's declared unit.

position_z.description: Height in the frame's declared unit, permitted only under a three-dimensional frame and optional even then. Null means the height is unknown rather than zero.

placement_role.description: What this microphone was for within the arrangement, when the caller declared a role. Free text, and null when none was declared.

orientation_description.description: Human-readable account of which way the microphone faced. Provenance for a reader, never applied by any computation.

source_profile_version_id.description: Device or setup profile version this placement was authored from, when one was cited. Recorded as provenance only: a reusable profile describes many sessions and cannot itself answer where a microphone was during this one.

notes.description: Free-text remarks about the placement. Never parsed by VAWLUME.

v_sequence_members.description: Sequence membership joined to its owning sequence, so an ordered event list can be read together with the analysis run, recording, epoch, and scope that define it without writing the join by hand.

relationships.description: Each configuration profile that names a project belongs to that project. A profile with no project is built in and applies to every project in the database.
Each registered version is a version of exactly one configuration profile. A profile accumulates versions over time and none of them replaces another.
Each project-level assignment names the exact profile version it assigns. The cited version cannot be deleted while the assignment stands.
Each project-level assignment names the project it applies to, and is removed with that project.
Each registered source file was discovered within one project, and its location is unique within that project rather than globally.
Each ingestion attempt names the exact mapping profile version that interpreted its sources, which is what makes the rows it produced traceable to the rules that produced them.
Each ingestion attempt is an attempt to ingest one project.
Each per-file outcome names the source file it reports on.
Each per-file outcome belongs to the ingestion attempt that produced it, so one file can have a different outcome in each attempt.
Each hierarchy level belongs to one project, because two projects may use the same native word for different levels.
Each entity records the ingestion attempt that first created it. Later compatible attempts leave this provenance alone and record their own audit rows instead.
Each entity sits at exactly one level of its project's hierarchy, and its native identifier is unique only within that level.
Each entity belongs to one project.
Each relationship may cite the source file it was read from, when it came from a single file.
Each relationship records the ingestion attempt that first created it, when it arose from one.
Names the contained or subordinate endpoint of the relationship. This is the child side; the parent side is a separate reference into the same table, and the two may not name the same entity.

Names the containing or superior endpoint of the relationship. This is the parent side, distinct from the child reference into the same table, and which endpoint is which is part of the relationship's meaning.
Each relationship belongs to the project both of its endpoints belong to.
Each attribute may cite the source file its value was read from.
Each attribute records the ingestion attempt that first created it, when it arose from one.
Each attribute describes exactly one entity and is removed with it.

Each recording is anchored to exactly one registered source file, and each such file backs at most one recording. This one-to-one anchor is the recording's durable identity and the boundary extractor imports resolve against.
Each recording belongs to one project.
Each channel belongs to exactly one recording, which is what makes anything attached to a channel specific to that session.
Each participation record names the ingestion attempt that first created it, when it arose from one.
Names the entity that took part in the recording.
Names the recording the entity took part in. One entity may be linked to one recording more than once under different roles or intervals.
Each attribute may cite the source file its value was read from.
Each attribute records the ingestion attempt that first created it, when it arose from one.
Each attribute describes exactly one recording and is removed with it.
Each entity-level assignment names the exact profile version it assigns. The cited version cannot be deleted while the assignment stands.
Each entity-level assignment names the entity it applies to, and is removed with that entity.
Each recording-level assignment names the exact profile version it assigns. The cited version cannot be deleted while the assignment stands.
Each recording-level assignment names the recording it applies to, whether the recording was given it directly or inherited it.
Each interval may cite the source file it was imported from, and cites none when it was declared directly.

Names the enclosing interval when this one is nested inside another of the same recording. A top-level interval names none, so the column is what distinguishes nesting depth rather than a separate level column.
Each interval falls within exactly one recording, and its bounds are seconds from that recording's start.
Each declared frame belongs to one project and is shared reference data within it.

Each placement may cite the device or setup profile version it was authored from. Provenance only: a reusable profile describes many sessions and does not itself assert where a microphone was during this one.

Each placement expresses its coordinates in exactly one declared frame, which must belong to the same project as the channel. A frame cannot be deleted while a placement still cites it, because coordinates in no declared space would be worse than refusing the delete.
Each placement positions exactly one channel's microphone, and a channel has at most one placement. A microphone moved mid-session is therefore unrepresentable rather than silently averaged.
